paths.description: Public overview archetype and main acquisition journey; tested desktop, mobile, dark mode, high contrast, reduced motion, no-JS, network, performance, accessibility, security, and memory.
Distinct feature-detail template for photo editing; tested desktop visual quality and mobile layout stability.
Primary conversion endpoint reached from Get the app; tested mobile task clarity and store-link availability.

findings.summary: The marketing pages do not adapt to the user’s dark colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains a white surface, and the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, control, and media treatments.

findings.summary: Reduced-motion users still receive smooth scrolling.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe matched reduce and found no running animations, but computed scroll-behavior remained smooth.
findings.suggestedFix: Set scroll-behavior: auto inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce in addition to shortening animation and transition durations.

findings.summary: Route changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no view-transition CSS or authored startViewTransition use while the header exposes navigation between overview and editing pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for same-origin marketing routes, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long-page reveal and scroll-linked presentation is not implemented with CSS scroll-driven animations.
findings.evidence: The 17,198px overview page uses in-view effects, while the CSS probe found no animation-timeline or scroll-timeline.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace scroll-listener-based reveal effects with view() or scroll() timelines where motion adds value.

findings.summary: Carousels use custom controls without platform scroll snapping or overscroll containment.
findings.evidence: The DOM exposes custom photos-scrollable carousels and the CSS probe found no scroll-snap or overscroll-behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll snap and overscroll containment for touch-friendly carousel movement, retaining labelled controls.

findings.summary: The fixed navigation does not react to scroll state on a very long page.
findings.evidence: The overview is 17,198px tall, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state container query or authored scroll progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrained scroll-state treatment, such as a compact header or section progress indicator.

findings.summary: The cookie notice obscures a large share of the first viewport.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show the cookie notice covering the bottom of the hero; on 360x800 it consumes roughly one third of the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, content-preserving consent surface while retaining equally prominent accept and reject actions.

findings.summary: Disclosure and carousel UI relies on custom elements instead of native disclosure primitives.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found no dialog, popover, or details elements, despite a large FAQ and multiple transient/custom carousel controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use details/summary for FAQs and native popover or dialog semantics where transient or modal UI is needed.

findings.summary: Reusable components adapt only through viewport media queries.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container rules despite cards, tiles, carousels, and navigation being reused across sizes.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable modules containment and use size-aware container queries for local layout changes.

findings.summary: Some interactive targets are too small or overlap another control.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse target-size auditing found the Magic Eraser link had only 13px of safe clickable spacing because an image-comparison range overlaps it; carousel dots are also only 8px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate overlapping controls and provide at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels of safe target area, preferably 44 by 44 for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: The initial load misses the good LCP threshold in the mobile lab run.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 3.2s, LCP 3.6s, Speed Index 5.5s, and TTI 8.5s. The independent trace measured LCP 2.33s, showing sensitivity to load conditions.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the entry redirect, prioritise the hero resource, and defer non-essential media and analytics to bring repeatable LCP below 2.5s.

findings.summary: A redirect and render-blocking resources delay the first render.
findings.evidence: HAR and Lighthouse identify the photos.google.com redirect, parser-blocking cookie script and styles, and about 1.0s potential savings from redirects and render blocking. Module scripts were confirmed deferred by type=module and are not counted as blockers.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve the canonical landing response directly, defer the cookie script, and reduce or inline only genuinely critical CSS.

findings.summary: Analytics bundles add substantial unused JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 187 KiB unused JavaScript across three Tag Manager and Analytics bundles, each 44% to 53% unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate analytics, load it after consent and idle time, and remove duplicate UA, GA4, and GTM paths.

findings.summary: Several controls expose conflicting or missing accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found visible-label/name mismatches on ten links, three role=img SVG search icons without names, and two images without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep visible link text in the accessible name, mark decorative SVGs hidden or name meaningful ones, and provide appropriate alt text.

findings.summary: Focusable carousel tabs are hidden from the accessibility tree.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse and the platform probe found three focusable tab buttons inside a ul with aria-hidden=true.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not place focusable descendants under aria-hidden; either expose the tablist correctly or remove its descendants from keyboard navigation.

findings.summary: Touch-target spacing fails in an interactive image comparison.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse target-size auditing found a link partially obscured by a large range input, leaving 13px safe spacing.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct stacking and hit regions, then verify at narrow viewports and 200% zoom.

findings.summary: Some image assets lack dimensions or render at the wrong aspect ratio.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 7 of 35 images without dimensions and Lighthouse failed the image aspect-ratio audit. Observed CLS stayed low but the authored asset contract is fragile.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide width and height or aspect-ratio for every image and preserve intrinsic proportions in CSS.

findings.summary: Seven links use generic “Learn more” text.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO auditing listed seven generic Learn more links, reducing destination clarity for crawlers and users.
findings.suggestedFix: Use destination-specific visible link labels such as “Learn about Magic Eraser” and “Google Photos safety”.

findings.summary: The entry URL’s canonical and hreflang signals conflict.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports that the canonical points to another hreflang location; the page redirects from photos.google.com to www.google.com/photos/about/ and then declares an en_uk canonical.
findings.suggestedFix: Align redirects, canonical, hreflang, sitemap, and locale URLs so each locale self-canonicalises consistently.

findings.summary: Analytics and tracking requests start before the user chooses consent.
findings.evidence: The load screenshot still shows the consent notice while trackers detected Google Tag Manager and two Google Analytics origins; HAR recorded 89 nominally cross-origin requests and 4.92 MB from those origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not initialise analytics until affirmative consent, consolidate trackers, and minimise events and retained identifiers.

findings.summary: Transport protection is incomplete despite HTTPS and CSP.
findings.evidence: The header probe found no HSTS and a CSP containing unsafe-eval; the only NID cookie was HttpOnly but not Secure and SameSite=None. The exposed Google API key is a public client key and was not treated as a secret.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS at the effective origin, remove unsafe-eval where possible, and ensure every cross-site cookie is Secure with the narrowest workable SameSite policy.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced policy headers are absent.
findings.evidence: The header probe found no frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy on the effective page response.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors, a restrictive Referrer-Policy, and a minimal Permissions-Policy; evaluate Trusted Types for the script-heavy surface.

findings.summary: The first viewport does not present the core hero correctly without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured 90% raw-text coverage, but the raw HTML had no H1 and the crawler screenshot showed a mostly blank first viewport with navigation only.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the complete hero heading and visible initial state, then layer animation and media enhancement after load.

findings.summary: The landing page ships a heavy image and media payload with large optimisation savings.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse transferred 5,903 KiB and estimated 1,044 KiB image-delivery savings; HAR recorded 3.32 MB of images, while 16 images lacked srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive AVIF or WebP variants, add srcset and sizes, and avoid loading below-fold media until it nears the viewport.

findings.summary: Background analytics and media work is disproportionate before interaction.
findings.evidence: HAR loaded 93 requests including 27 scripts and 19 media requests; analytics alone shipped over 400 KB, with 187 KiB estimated unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritise background fetches, gate analytics on consent, and fetch media on viewport proximity or explicit play.

findings.summary: Third-party fonts, analytics, images, and media dominate the transfer budget.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes 4.92 MB of 4.92 MB to nominal cross-origin hosts, including 3.31 MB images, 745 KB fonts, and 406 KB Tag Manager.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a page-weight budget, self-host or subset fonts where appropriate, consolidate analytics, and lazily fetch heavy media.
